verdict.headline: Rey Cortiço Mid-morning — 11:00
verdict.reason: Rey Cortiço is worth a quick check for mid-morning — 11:00, but it is not a guaranteed session.  Treat it as a check-first call rather than a sure thing.  Wind is the main thing to watch.  The tide should let the sandbars work without overdoing it.

conversationalSummary.text: For TODAY, Rey Cortiço around mid-morning is the best available shot, but it’s a rare window and the wind angle isn’t ideal for that spot. I’d check the Surfline cams (and MEO Beachcam for backup) before you head out, because the swell consistency looks shaky and the sandbanks can change fast. If the cams aren’t showing it much cleaner than expected, I’d rather save the session—wind could easily make it messy.

best.explanation: Rey Cortiço looks like a fun-sized north coast window for Rare window, Medium confidence: 0.6-0.9 m, 63 kJ, 8 s period, lully 26/100, and wind is the main risk.  An open beach break where the sandbanks decide everything; this is best for quiet, punchy peaks when Lagide is too small; 6-9s at low tide can still work on Belgas if the sandbars are lined up, so checking exposed beaches makes sense.  Watch: Surfline consistency is lully; wind angle is poor for this spot.
